LPDDR6 on-die ECC (ODECC) is mandatory per JESD209-6 (unlike LPDDR5 where it was optional). Our EDAC driver is logging a rising count of correctable single-bit errors concentrated on one sub-channel:

  EDAC DRAM: Correctable ECC error, page=0x123456, syndrome=0x42
  EDAC DRAM: Correctable ECC error count 5000 in 60s, sub-channel=2

No uncorrectable errors yet. Is this a warranty-return indicator? What MR (mode register) exposes the error counter, and how should the driver integrate with Linux drivers/edac/ to support page offlining before UEs occur? When does LPDDR6 differ from LPDDR5X handling here?
